title: 15. Influence of hide color and ranch source on behavior, feed efficiency, and carcass traits in beef steers.
content:
Abstract
Behavior and temperament have been shown to impact beef cattle production traits. Our objective was to assess chute exit velocity, activity, carcass data, and feed efficiency based on hide color, ranch source, and quality grade. Steers from a commercial ranch (n = 57) were studied for 147 d on Vytelle SENSE for feed intake. Body weights were collected every 2 weeks. These data were utilized to calculate intake, average daily gain (ADG), residual feed intake (RFI), and feed conversion ratio (FCR). Mounting and activity were measured using 701xPro tags and carcass data was collected at a commercial abattoir. Data were analyzed using the GLM procedure of SAS (v.9.04) with fixed effects of hide color, ranch source, and quality grade. Response variables include chute velocity at initial, mid-, and final time points, activity and mounting behavior, carcass characteristics, and feed efficiency. Alpha was set at 0.05. Steers sourced from division A ranch have higher heart scores (P < 0.0001) than all other divisions and division B (P < 0.01) had higher heart scores than division C and division D which do not differ (P = 0.56). Red hided steers had a tendency (P = 0.06) to have a higher chute velocity at midpoint than black hided steers. Feed intake tended (P = 0.08) to differ between ranch sources, but no independent variable were significantly different (P = 0.18). Initial weight tended (P = 0.08) to differ by ranch source (P = 0.04). Final weight differed (P = 0.05) where weights differed (P = 0.02) by ranch source. Ranch source was the most common factor influencing metrics of growth and heart score, whereas hide color was the predominant factor influencing chute exit velocity. Future analyses and alternative models may be able to further investigate the impact of behavior and temperament on carcass metrics. USDA is an equal opportunity provider and employer.
